extracted.intended_audience: students, editors, and scholars working on Euclid's Data / classical geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly notes and editorial guidance for correcting, reordering, and explaining Euclid's Data (definitions, propositions, demonstrations), with recommendations for translation, omitted/added propositions, and constructive/constructibility constraints. Intended to guide editors and students in producing a usable edition and to assist beginners in deriving constructions from analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition IV (given in position) — must be constructible
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have amended [def. 4] by adding, 'and which are either actually exhibited or can be found; for nothing is to be reckoned given, which cannot be found, or is not actually exhibited.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat a line/point as 'given in position' merely because it is invariable; it must be actually exhibited or constructible by the Elements. Example: BD (the seventh-part construction) would be invariable but cannot be found by Euclid's Elements, so it should not be 'given'. This amendment prevents counting unconstructible objects as given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'given' — geometric vs arithmetic
rubrics_metrics.description: The Data are to be understood to be given geometrically, not always arithmetically, that is, they cannot always be exhibited in numbers; e.g., the ratio of the side of a square to its diameter is given geometrically, but not in numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stating something is 'given' in the Data, treat it as a geometric relation/ratio or position rather than assuming a numeric/arithmetic representation is available. Be explicit when numeric exhibition is not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on propositions that assume finding proportional magnitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Euclid assumes 'because A is given, a magnitude equal to it can be found' or that a 'ratio which is the same can be found', there must be an added limitation: the magnitudes/ratios referred to must be actually findable by the Elements; otherwise the proposition is not demonstrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add explicit limitations when a proof relies on constructing a fourth proportional or finding a magnitude with a given ratio; otherwise the logical step is invalid. Example: Prop. II depends on such an assumption and needs the additional limitation to be correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not count a ratio as given merely by showing equality to another non-exhibited ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: It is absurd to take a ratio as given if it is only shown to be equal to another ratio which itself is not found; given must mean actually exhibited/found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the modern/editorial mistake (and errors by Newton) of treating 'given ratios' and 'always-the-same ratios' as identical. Ensure the ratio is exhibited or constructible, not just provably equal to some other unexhibited ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering and grouping of propositions for naturalness and usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorder propositions so that simpler ones precede more complex ones and group together propositions of the same kind (e.g., move prop. 12 to be the 5th; make 22/23 into 11/12 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing, change the sequence to improve pedagogical flow and to place frequently used propositions before those that depend on them; this helps readers and beginners derive constructions from analyses more readily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit or adapt definitions/propositions that are unusable in translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions XI and XII (and some others) are omitted because they cannot be given in English so as to have tolerable sense; similarly the 13th–15th are omitted as being of no use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a term/definition cannot be faithfully and usefully rendered in the target language, consider omitting it and substitute the explanatory words where needed, rather than retaining an incomprehensible literal translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore/add frequently useful propositions missing from the Greek
rubrics_metrics.description: Add propositions that are necessary or frequently useful but absent in the Greek text (e.g., props. 21 omitted in Greek but needed; props. 37 and 41 added; props. 62, 58, 59 added or adjusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the corpus by inserting propositions and demonstrations which are essential for later results; demonstrate them explicitly rather than leaving dependencies unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine or split propositions to reflect identical enunciations/demonstrations or to separate cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine propositions when the same enunciation/demonstration serves both (e.g., Greek 35 & 36 joined), and split when distinctness aids clarity (e.g., prop. 70 divided into 67 & 68).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit structural grouping to reduce redundancy and to clarify separate cases; ensure enunciations and demonstrations align after changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add determinations and explicit cases where the Greek is deficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide determinations and explicitly give the different cases that were omitted in the Greek (e.g., props. 34/36, 48 have explicit cases added).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a proposition has multiple geometrical cases, list and demonstrate each explicitly to avoid hidden assumptions in the original text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer citing appropriate prior propositions instead of redoing standard algebraic steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conclusion follows directly by a previously proved proposition, cite that proposition rather than using inversion/composition steps (e.g., prop. 16 should cite prop. 6; other examples cite props. 7, 23, 22 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make demonstrations concise and formally correct by invoking the simplest applicable earlier results; it both shortens proofs and clarifies logical dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct erroneous translations and restore intended Greek meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful of translator errors (e.g., Hardy/Gregory misrendered 'ftu ry; eivmi h'); restore correct sense (e.g., ratios mentioned 'must not be the same' — 'non autem easdem').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Greek originals and multiple manuscripts; do not follow earlier translators unquestioningly. Where prior translations conflict or yield absurdities, clarify with the correct rendering and explain the impact on the propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter enunciations arbitrarily without adjusting demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposition's enunciation is changed (e.g., prop. 86 as handled by Gregory), its demonstration must be correspondingly adjusted; do not change enunciation and leave the old demonstration intact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing, ensure internal consistency: any change to enunciation, order, or content must propagate to the demonstration and corollaries or add new supporting propositions instead of overwriting needed ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure existence claims in constructions are proved
rubrics_metrics.description: When the text asserts that a certain constructed line meets a figure (e.g., a parallel meets the circumference) or that three lines satisfy triangle inequalities, these meet/existence facts should be explicitly demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume geometric existence without proof in the demonstration. Provide the missing steps (e.g., show that the parallel KL meets the circumference in the figure for prop. 77, or that three constructed lines satisfy the triangle inequality as required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include propositions/corollaries for similar-figure cases not given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: Add propositions (e.g., prop. 58) showing that results about figures given in species hold for similar figures even when not given in species, since such cases frequently occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend Data to cover practical cases encountered in problem-solving by proving corollaries so users can apply results to a broader set of figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explicit examples connecting analysis to construction for beginners
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the construction part of a problem may not be readily deduced from the analysis by beginners, include detailed examples showing derivation of each construction step from the analysis (example provided for parallelogram problem derived from prop. 87 analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include worked examples that trace how ratios/rectangles/squares stated in analysis are manifested in the construction; this aids novices in applying the Data to problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer shorter, corrected demonstrations when Greek ones are vitiated
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Greek demonstration is grossly vitiated (e.g., prop. 73), replace it with a corrected shorter demonstration, citing appropriate earlier propositions (prop. 23 instead of 22, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reproduce clearly faulty proofs; supply corrected, logically valid demonstrations that follow Elements' methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: When adding propositions, place them so they serve subsequent proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert frequently used propositions early enough to be used by later propositions (e.g., add prop. 62 because it is necessary to props. 86–88 and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the sequence so dependencies are satisfied; avoid leaving later proofs dependent on missing lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about the types of ratios and what operations produce given ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: When the text states that certain ratios are 'given' by inversion/composition/permutation, be precise about which operations are used and when standard propositions (prop. 6,7, etc.) justify the step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implicit algebraic steps; indicate when inversion, composition, permutation, or conversion is applied and cite the supporting proposition to validate that the resulting ratio is 'given'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial principle: keep the Data usable rather than faithful to corrupted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Although order has been changed from former editions, this is acceptable because ancient geometers rarely cite the Data; prioritize usability over slavish adherence to corrupted Greek order/text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When manuscripts are defective or careless, produce an edition that is coherent and usable for modern readers even if it diverges from a particular Greek ordering; document changes and justifications in notes.
